name: Lucas Barbosa dos Santos
bio1: Full-stack developer and Multiplatform Software Development student at Fatec Itaquera. My journey in technology is driven by a passion for creating functional solutions and the ambition to become a Game Developer.
bio2: With a strong interest in Design and UX/UI, I always seek to merge code with an intuitive and visually impactful user experience in my projects.
softSkill1_desc: Ability to collaborate with other developers and designers to achieve common goals.
softSkill2_desc: Focus on analyzing complex challenges, identifying causes, and implementing efficient and robust solutions.
softSkill3_desc: Initiative to anticipate problems, seek continuous improvements, and learn new technologies.
extra2_desc: Knowledge in image editing, asset creation, and layout manipulation for web projects.
exp1_company: Faculdade de Tecnologia de Itaquera - FATEC Itaquera
exp1_desc: Internal internship provided by the college to gain work experience and assist in the institution's development. I developed and maintained RESTful APIs in PHP and MySQL for managing academic events and extension courses on the institution's portal, ensured integrity for new features, improving the registration flow and course visualization, and used Postman for testing, validation, and documentation of API routes, ensuring data integrity.

proj1_shortDesc: Frontend of a platform to connect NGOs to volunteers.
proj1_longDesc: Interdisciplinary project from the second semester of the Multiplatform Software Development course. I worked on the front-end and its connection to the backend using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The project consists of a platform to connect NGOs to volunteers, where NGOs can recruit and promote themselves, and volunteers can sign up to participate and work together with the NGOs.
proj2_shortDesc: Dashboard for immigrant advisory, with frontend and backend integration.
proj2_longDesc: Interdisciplinary project from the third semester of the Multiplatform Software Development course, featuring a robust backend in Spring, where I worked on the frontend and its interaction with the backend. The project is a dashboard for immigrant advisory, designed for the advisory to have an easy registration of clients and their data, and to have clear information about them and their needs.
proj3_shortDesc: Reimagining of Conecta ONGS, with a full-stack stack in Node.JS and React.
proj3_longDesc: Interdisciplinary project from the fourth semester of the Multiplatform Software Development course. I worked full-stack on this project, using Node.JS and React, which is a reconstruction of the second-semester project. It was recreated to better achieve its goals and to be more modern, with a more current stack. The project is a platform with social media aspects for easy visualization of an NGO's needs and goals. With this, users can connect with NGOs and sign up to participate in their activities. The project focuses on being a platform with easy access and use, and being visually pleasing to encourage user engagement with the NGOs.
proj4_shortDesc: Mobile game key store, using the IGDB API.
proj4_longDesc: Interdisciplinary project from the fifth semester of the Multiplatform Software Development course. I worked on the Frontend using React Native. I also worked using the IGDB API for easy access to game data. This project is a mobile game key store where users can browse a game catalog, see details about them, and buy keys for them. The project focuses on being a platform with easy access and use, and being visually pleasing. The store uses the IGDB API for easy access to game data, so a potential shopkeeper only needs to worry about selling keys, not about obtaining game data, and to keep game data always updated.
proj5_shortDesc: Small demonstration of an RPG game developed by me in Unity.
proj5_longDesc: Game developed in Unity where you can explore a small map, interact, and face enemies in turn-based battles. It was a personal project to develop my game development skills. The game consists of a simple loop of facing enemies and being rewarded for it. The battles, being turn-based, have a tactical system that does not give direct control over all party members, but rather indirect control, where the player can choose actions for the party members, but not exactly what each one does. Upon defeating each enemy, the player is rewarded with more attacks in their arsenal, and other party members, as they evolve, gain their own moves to have larger roles in battle. The game focuses on being a small demonstration of an RPG game and is not intended to be a complete game, but rather a project to develop my game development skills.
